newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended higher as the market waited for new Swiss federal bond issues due to be auctioned on September 26.

"People were positioning ahead of the new Confederate bond issue," said one Swiss trader at the close. Traders expected a longer tranche and a medium-term offering which would be deliverable against the new "Comi" bond contract.

In the longer tranche, the trader did not rule out a switch to reopen a bond maturing in 2008, instead of reopening a 2006 maturity. The 10-year 4-1/2 percent April 2006 benchmark is now relatively expensive for investors, he said.
There was also massive switching out of the 2006 benchmark on Friday, possibly into the 4-1/4 percent January 2008 bond.
This may have also accounted for a huge volume traded in the April 2006, estimated at 85 million Swiss francs on the exchange and an additional 50 to 60 million off-exchange.
Markets were meanwhile less inclined to expect any further interest rate cuts in Germany after news Thursday of slightly higher M3 growth in August of an annualised 8.7 percent.
Participants were also waiting for the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday. Markets remain uncertain about whether the Fed will opt to raise its discount rate.
Dec conf futures CONFZ6 up 15 at 114.35
Dec comi medium-term bond COMIZ6 up two at 109.90.
Dec Euro Swiss francs FESZ6 up nine at 98.15.
